Records that the window's latest frame was presented between `present_start`
and `present_end`.

`window_active` says whether the window is active, and `next_frame_scheduled`
says whether another frame is already requested. Together they decide whether
the gap until the next newly drawn frame counts as an animation interval.

d.2:40:
Returns an incident when the snapshot contains at least one event
that blocked the foreground for `threshold` or longer, or when the
interval's total foreground spend — event time plus folded
small-poll time — reached `frame_budget` even though no single event
did. In the latter case every event in the interval becomes a
contributor, since no single stall explains the busy interval.

d.1:3:
Recolors `count` distinct seeded random descendants in one pass and notifies each
affected entity boundary once (the root, for descendants owned by no entity).
Returns how many descendants changed and how many boundaries were notified.

This is the "share of the scene changing per frame" knob: `count` calls to
[`Self::apply_mutation`] would each walk the tree and notify separately, costing
more than the frame being measured once `count` is a fair share of the tree.

d.4:3:
Translates a drag from a source item to an insertion slot into the final
`(from, to)` index pair, or `None` when the move is a no-op or out of range.

An insertion slot sits *between* items (`0..=len`); when the slot is past the
source the target shifts down by one to account for the source being lifted
out first. This is the canonical reorder index math shared by every sortable
list so virtualized (delegate) and data-driven lists agree on what a drop
means.

Creates an opaque [`Rgba`] color from a `0xRRGGBB` hex number.

The highest byte of `hex` is ignored, and the alpha is `1.0`. Use [`rgba`] for a color
with alpha.

# Examples

```
use gpui::rgb;

assert_eq!(rgb(0xffffff).alpha, 1.0);
```
